Weighted 2D histogram

Source: R/kernel-smoothing.R
hist.weighted.2D.Rd

2D analogue of hist.weighted(): bins (x, y) pairs into a grid defined by x.breaks/y.breaks and sums weight within each cell.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'weighted.2D'
hist(x, y, weight, x.breaks, y.breaks)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric vectors of coordinates to bin (same length).

weight

Numeric vector of weights, same length as x/y.

x.breaks, y.breaks

Numeric vectors of bin edges for each dimension; must span the range of x/y respectively (an error otherwise).

Value

A list with x.breaks, y.breaks, x.mids, y.mids, counts (matrix of summed weight per cell), and density (counts normalised to integrate to 1 over the grid).

A note on the name

As with hist.weighted(), this is an ordinary function rather than an S3 method for graphics::hist(), and needs an explicit @rawNamespace export directive for that reason.

References

D'Angelo et al. (2024); see spHawkes-package.

Examples

h <- hist.weighted.2D(
  x = c(0.2, 0.7, 1.5), y = c(0.1, 0.9, 1.2), weight = c(1, 2, 1),
  x.breaks = 0:2, y.breaks = 0:2
)
h$density
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,] 0.75 0.00
#> [2,] 0.00 0.25
